items.title: The New York Times, 9 October 1903, page 6 (editorial 'Flying Machines Which Do Not Fly')
items.holder: Internet Archive (Serials in Microfilm scan, item sim_new-york-times_1903-10-09_53_16774)
items.rights: public domain by date (INFERRED: the holder gives no rights statement)
items.rights_statement: No rights field in the item record. Published in the US in 1903, so out of US copyright.
items.credit_line: The New York Times, 9 October 1903, p. 6. Scan: Internet Archive.
items.notes: Checked by eye: this is page 6, running head reads THE NEW YORK TIMES, FRIDAY, OCTOBER 9, 1903. Highest resolution offered (single-page JP2, 400 ppi microfilm scan). Approximate boxes in full-res pixels (x0,y0,x1,y1): running head with date 2394,518,4612,596; headline FLYING MACHINES WHICH DO NOT / FLY. 2180,4940,3015,5040 (column 3); 'from one million to ten million' 3250,3125,3905,3155 (column 4); 'years' is the first word of the NEXT line at 3070,3180,3180,3210, so the phrase breaks across two lines and a pencil underline needs two strokes. Body type is about 20 px tall: legible, soft and grainy at a 4K macro, which suits the scanline pass. Greyscale. Internet Archive terms of use say access is granted for scholarship and research; that is a site term, not a copyright in a 1903 newspaper.

items.title: Notebook by Alexander Graham Bell, from 1875 to 1876: pages 40-41, entry of 10 March 1876 (image 22)
items.holder: Library of Congress, Manuscript Division (Alexander Graham Bell Family Papers)
items.rights: public domain (stated by the holder)
items.rights_statement: All manuscripts that Alexander Graham Bell and his descendants wrote are in the public domain.
items.credit_line: Library of Congress, Manuscript Division, Alexander Graham Bell Family Papers at the Library of Congress
items.notes: Checked by eye: the double-page spread, page numbers 40 and 41, headed 'March 10th 1876', with the Fig. 1 sketch of the transmitter (M, P, W, S). 4080x2475 greyscale master TIFF. The sentence starts on the last line of p. 40 and finishes on the first line of p. 41. As written by Bell: sentence: "Mr. Watson - Come here - I want to [page turn] see you". Details: opening double quote before Mr; the r of Mr is raised with a short stroke under it and there is no full stop on the line after it; long dashes after Watson and after here; Come is written with a tall capital C and runs almost into here; no comma, no exclamation mark; the closing quote comes straight after you and the full stop is written AFTER the closing quote. Lower on p. 41 Watson's repeat is written with a small c: 'Mr. Watson - come here - I want to see you'. Approximate boxes in full-res pixels: date 650,180,1320,290; first sentence on p. 40 150,2180,2080,2475; continuation on p. 41 2180,180,4040,420.

items.title: Sperm whale clicks (Physeter macrocephalus), file Phma-clicks-NOAA-PAGroup-01
items.event_date: published 2023 (recording date and place not given)
items.holder: NOAA Fisheries, Northeast Fisheries Science Center, Passive Acoustics Branch
items.rights: US Government work: not subject to US copyright (stated by the holder for NOAA-created material)
items.rights_statement: Information created by the U.S. government and presented on U.S. government websites is not subject to copyright in the United States.
items.credit_line: NOAA. NOAA Fisheries, NEFSC, Passive Acoustics Branch. 2023. Sperm Whale. (or: Courtesy: National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration)
items.notes: Not listened to: measured. 6.37 s, mono, 48 kHz MP3 (the only format offered). A crude peak count finds about 20 clicks in three bursts: a fast run of about 10 clicks from 0.23 to 0.87 s (gaps 0.05-0.13 s), six evenly spaced clicks from 2.13 to 2.96 s (gaps about 0.16 s), and four evenly spaced clicks from 5.33 to 5.78 s (gaps about 0.15 s). NO 1+1+3 coda: none of the bursts has two slow clicks followed by three fast ones, and NOAA's New England recordings would not be expected to carry that Caribbean pattern. Single clean clicks can be lifted from the second and third bursts. The policy 'encourages' non-commercial, scientific and educational use; that sentence is encouragement, not a restriction, since the same paragraph says the material is not subject to copyright. A second NOAA clip exists as video: 'Sperm Whale Clicks and Buzz', 0:22, 2025 survey, https://videos.fisheries.noaa.gov/detail/video/6398002997112/sperm-whale-clicks-and-buzz (not downloaded).
